tone_statements.citation: de Sousa, Hilário. 2016. Pínghuà (of Guǎngxī). In Sybesma et al. (eds.), Encyclopedia of Chinese Language and Linguistics, vol. 3, 425-431. Leiden: Brill.
tone_statements.quote: In contrast, the phonology of Northern Pínghuà has been Mandarinized: -m -p -t -k no longer exist, and there are fewer tones (but still more tones than the four or five tones in the Southwestern Mandarin spoken in Guǎngxī). ... The following are some phonological traits commonly found in Northern Pínghuà dialects. ... – The plosive codas of Middle Chinese are turned into a glottal stop, or dropped all together; usually at least one entering tone is retained as a separate toneme; ... – One rising (shǎng 上) tone; – Systematic tone-sandhi.
tone_statements.locator: author's draft pp. 1-2 (opening section) and p. 6 (section 'Phonological difference between Southern and Northern Pínghuà', list of Northern Pinghua traits); published version = ECLL vol. 3, pp. 425-431
tone_statements.summary: Tonal Sinitic variety group: Northern Pinghua dialects have fewer tones than Southern Pinghua (which keeps 6 codas and at least three entering tones) but more than the four or five of Guangxi Southwestern Mandarin; Middle Chinese stop codas are reduced to a glottal stop or lost, yet usually at least one entering (rù) tone survives as a separate toneme; one shǎng (rising) tone category; systematic…

tone.says: Northern Pinghua is 'Mandarinized' - stop codas lost, fewer tones than Southern Pinghua but more than the 4-5 of Guangxi SW Mandarin; common Northern traits listed include at least one entering tone usually kept as a separate toneme, a single shang (rising) tone category, and systematic tone sandhi (Southern Pinghua: 'no systematic tone-sandhi'). No tone values for a Northern point; nothing on stress.
